newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian cinema chain Kinepolis eyes stock listing.
newsitem.headline: Belgian cinema chain Kinepolis eyes stock listing.

text.p: Belgian multiplex cinema chain Kinepolis is likely to seek a bourse listing in the autumn, one of the group's leading minority shareholders said on Friday.

"It is being looked at, for the autumn...If all conditions stay right you can say that the chance (of a listing) is fairly big," said Gerard Van Acker, managing director of GIMV, the investment company of Belgium's Flemish regional government.
"We're working on it... It's a bit quieter because of the holidays, but it will be actively followed up again in mid-August," he told Reuters.

Van Acker said Kinepolis, which is majority-owned by Belgium's Bert and Claeys families, was likely to be listed on the Brussels bourse. A listing on the Easdaq growth stocks market was also being considered, but was less likely.
The Bert family was not available for comment, and a spokesman for the Claeys group declined to comment.

Van Acker said GIMV, which has a 23.77 percent stake in Kinepolis, would decide in September or October whether to sell part of its own stake in Kinepolis, which runs multiplex cinemas in the Belgian cities of Brussels, Antwerp and Hasselt and also operates in France.
Van Acker said the listing was not linked to the financing needs of Kinepolis's expansion plans in Spain.
"That project has already been financed," he said.
GIMV has taken a 30 percent stake in Group Claeys' 1.2 billion franc ($31.5 million) Kinepolis project in Madrid, which is to become the world's largest cinema multiplex when it opens in late 1998.
Several large Belgian banks were now bidding for the right to manage the listing. "This has become typical on the Belgian market. We have experienced it ourselves," Van Acker said.
GIMV floated 19.9 percent of its capital on the Brussels bourse in June.

The Kinepolis group -- whose Brussels multiplex was the first of the giant cinema complexes now common in Europe -- had a 1996 consolidated turnover of 1.52 billion francs and net profit of 96 million francs. It had 5.4 million visitors.
Kinepolis is expecting a further rise in net profit and cash flow in 1997, GIMV said in its 1996 annual report.
